pairs.subject: offer-lifecycle-and-deadlines
pairs.evidence: app/offer/[token]/kit/OfferKitView.tsx:98 On a lapsed offer the page still renders the 'prepared for' name and the compensation strip, and the expired card gives no expiry date. The technique says the lapsed answer must name the role and the date but never the candidate or their terms.

techniques.evidence: app/offer/[token]/kit/OfferKitView.tsx:98 Unknown (404 invalidLink card), expired and load-failure each get their own card, which is correct. But the expired phase still shows the salary StatStrip and the preparedFor name (line 96). The expired copy (line 112, expiredBody) also never says when the offer expired.

app/offer/[token]/kit/OfferKitDecision.tsx:43 Mostly realized: the hours figure is computed on the server (OfferClient.tsx:30), the page revalidates on focus and on an interval (OfferClient.tsx:172), the deadline is shown as an absolute date with a named zone, and decline goes through an inline alertdialog that lands focus on Go back first. Missing: the 'units by proximity' rule. The page shows only hours or minutes, so a 7-day offer reads '168 hours left' from the day it is sent, with no days unit and no holding back of the countdown until the last stretch.

app/offer/[token]/OfferClient.tsx:183 The client one-in-flight guard is only manners. Correctness is the store's compare-and-swap (CAS). After an ambiguous POST the page re-reads the authoritative state (refresh), and an alreadyResponded 200 settles to the success card instead of showing an error.

pairs.subject: offer-lifecycle-and-deadlines
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/offer-finalize.ts:35 An accept or decline sent after the deadline gets a 410 (via route.ts:61), but nothing records that the candidate tried, so no recruiter task is raised. The technique says a submit against a lapsed offer must be recorded and routed to a person, not only refused.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/offer-finalize.ts:35 The 404-versus-410 split is correct (route.ts:29 and :61), lapse is checked on read (offerView runs expireOfferIfDue), and tokens carry 192 bits of randomness. But the late attempt is never recorded (a grep for late-attempt terms found nothing). The GET projection of an expired offer also still includes candidateLabel (offer-finalize.ts:220) and salary.

app/_lib/offers-store.ts:387 A single conditional write decides the winner, and side effects run only on the claimed branch. Lapse is checked before accept (offer-finalize.ts:29). The loser gets the recorded state as success, or expired, and never falls through to 'declined'. The hire meter is keyed on crossing into the terminal stage. Metering is debited, never used as a gate.

app/_lib/offer-finalize.ts:227 Remaining time comes from the server clock that enforces expiry, rounded up and clamped at zero (offer-policy.ts). The time zone is projected from the server, and the value is null when there is no deadline.
